note: Naming intervals by ear in two stages of the game: every interval up to the 6ths, then all twelve. The answers are named as the game's buttons show them, with the plain word beside each the first time; the text says what the next stage adds and how a stage feels before the next, and names the Stage selector, never a chip.

exercise.title: Name the interval you hear
exercise.why: A leap you can name by ear is a leap you can aim your voice at, so hearing the gap first is half of singing it in tune.

cells.text:
Press Start in the game below: it plays two notes, one after the other. Pick the interval's name from the buttons, such as m3 for a minor 3rd, P5 for a perfect 5th or M6 for a major 6th. Press Next for the next one.
When the name comes before you have to sing the gap in your head, try the next stage: it adds m7, M7 and TT, the tritone, so all twelve are asked. Use the Stage selector below to change the stage, then press Start in the game again.
If a stage turns into guessing, go back one stage.
